full_name: Brendan Iribe Center for Computer Science & Engineering
description: Home of UMD's CS department, featuring modern research labs, collaborative study spaces, and the grand atrium. Named after Brendan Iribe, co-founder of Oculus VR.
address: 8125 Paint Branch Dr, College Park, MD 20742

full_name: Edward St. John Learning & Teaching Center
description: A large multi-purpose academic building with lecture halls, classrooms, and collaborative spaces used across many departments.
Home of UMD's College of Information Studies and non-print media collections. Contains group study rooms, the Maryland Room archives, and the Broadcasting, Journalism & Media Collection.
UMD's main research library with millions of volumes, quiet study floors, group rooms, and the McKeldin Terrace overlooking the fountain. The go-to spot for finals week.
The heart of campus life. Houses dining, the university bookstore, student org offices, a game room, Adele's coffee, and the main ballroom used for events and concerts.
Houses the Department of Chemistry & Biochemistry with undergraduate and graduate teaching labs, research facilities, and lecture halls.

department: Robert H. Smith School of Business
description: Home of the Robert H. Smith School of Business. Features trading rooms, case study halls, and the Dean's suite. Named after UMD alumnus Herman van Munching.

department: A. James Clark School of Engineering
description: State-of-the-art engineering building opened in 2017. Home to bioengineering, aerospace, and mechanical engineering programs. Features cutting-edge research labs and a sky bridge connecting to Kim Engineering.
address: 8278 Paint Branch Dr, College Park, MD 20742

description: Houses the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering along with the Institute for Advanced Computer Studies. Connected to the CS complex via walkways.
address: 8223 Paint Branch Dr, College Park, MD 20742

description: The primary classroom building for CS courses. Home to undergraduate CS labs, help center office hours, and large lecture halls for intro CS courses.
address: 8169 Paint Branch Dr, College Park, MD 20742

description: Home of the Department of Physics with research labs, lecture halls, and the observatory. Named after former UMD president John S. Toll.

department: A. James Clark School of Engineering
description: A major engineering hub housing Civil, Environmental, and Mechanical Engineering departments. Connected to A. James Clark Hall and features the Dean's office for the Clark School.
address: 8228 Paint Branch Dr, College Park, MD 20742

description: UMD's premier performing arts venue with concert halls, recital studios, and theater spaces. Home of the School of Music, School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies.
UMD's main arena seating 17,950. Home to Terp basketball and volleyball. Also hosts major concerts and campus-wide events like commencement.
address: 8500 Paint Branch Dr, College Park, MD 20742
hours: Event days only — check athletics schedule

description: UMD's main student recreation facility. Features an aquatic center, weight room, basketball courts, racquetball courts, and group fitness studios.
Houses the College of Education along with university administration offices. Named after Marie Mount, former dean of the College of Home Economics.
Central administrative hub housing the offices of the President, Provost, and key university leadership. Also contains the Registrar and Financial Aid offices.
Home of the School of Languages, Literatures & Cultures with classrooms and faculty offices for language and literature programs.
Joint home of the Departments of Biology and Psychology. Contains research labs, lecture halls, and the well-known large psychology lecture auditorium.
Houses the Department of Art History and Archaeology along with College of Arts & Humanities administrative offices. Named after Francis Scott Key, author of the Star-Spangled Banner.
Home of the Department of Government and Politics. Houses faculty offices, seminar rooms, and political science research centers.
Modern research complex connecting the Chemistry and Physics departments with shared instrumentation facilities and cutting-edge research labs.
Home of UMD's School of Public Health with programs in epidemiology, health behavior, family science, and kinesiology.
Home of the University of Maryland Alumni Association. A premier event and conference venue on campus used for receptions, ceremonies, and alumni gatherings.
Houses the Department of Materials Science and Engineering and the Institute for Research in Electronics and Applied Physics (IREAP).
Houses several College of Agriculture & Natural Resources departments including the Institute of Applied Agriculture.
Houses the Department of Music along with practice rooms, rehearsal spaces, and faculty studios. Primary home for music students prior to Clarice.
Houses the Department of English and several other humanities programs. Home to the writing center and English language teaching programs.
One of the oldest buildings on campus, originally built as a tavern in 1798. Now operated by Dining Services as an event and catering venue.
Historic arena built in 1931, home to UMD's gymnastics and wrestling teams. One of the oldest athletic facilities on campus.
Cultural and community center for Black students at UMD. Hosts performances, speakers, cultural celebrations, and student support programs. Nyumburu means 'freedom' in Swahili.
Home of the Philip Merrill College of Journalism, featuring a state-of-the-art newsroom, broadcast studios, and the Capital News Service bureau.
Houses the Department of Cell Biology and Molecular Genetics along with life sciences research labs and the Maryland Pathogen Research Institute.
Modern research facility for life sciences with advanced laboratories for biological, biochemical, and molecular research programs.

Home of the Department of Mathematics, with classrooms, seminar rooms, and tutoring spaces. Renamed in 2017 for William “Brit” Kirwan, former UMD president and University System of Maryland chancellor.
Classroom and office building on McKeldin Mall, home to the Department of Communication and the Department of Philosophy.
Administrative home of the College of Agriculture & Natural Resources (AGNR), on the north side of McKeldin Mall.
Home of the College of Education, with classrooms, counseling labs, and research centers for teaching and human development.
Home of the School of Architecture, Planning & Preservation, with design studios, the architecture library, and exhibition space.

Shared home of the Department of Art and the Department of Sociology, including studio spaces and the University of Maryland Art Gallery. Named for Parren J. Mitchell, Maryland's first African American member of Congress.
One of the main homes of the A. James Clark School of Engineering, with classrooms, teaching labs, and engineering student services on the Engineering quad.
Labs and classrooms for chemical and biomolecular engineering — also home to the Maryland University Training Reactor, the campus's small research reactor.
Home of the Department of Geology, with teaching labs and mineral and fossil collections, part of the College of Computer, Mathematical, and Natural Sciences.
Houses plant science, entomology, and landscape architecture programs, with teaching labs and nearby research greenhouses.
Lab and classroom building for microbiology and life sciences courses, part of the science cluster near the Chemistry Building.
Home of the Office of the Registrar and other student administrative services — transcripts, enrollment verification, and records. Named for civil rights leader Clarence M. Mitchell, Jr.
Houses the Graduate School and the Office of Student Financial Aid, next to the Main Administration Building.
One of campus's older halls (pronounced “Tolliver”), home to offices and programs in the College of Arts & Humanities.
Classroom and office building on south campus used by arts and humanities programs, including art studio spaces.
Home to humanities departments including American Studies and the Harriet Tubman Department of Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies.
The oldest academic building still in use on campus (1898) and the only academic building to survive the Great Fire of 1912.
Home of the University Counseling Center, offering free counseling, psychological services, and academic support for students.
Historic armory on the north end of McKeldin Mall, used for large lectures, exams, and ROTC programs. Named for Major General Milton Reckord.
Home of the University Visitor Center on Route 1 — the starting point for campus tours and prospective student visits.
Non-denominational chapel hosting weddings, memorial services, and religious life programs, surrounded by the Garden of Reflection and Remembrance on the hill above Route 1.
Student medical services including primary care, mental health, and a pharmacy, located right next to Stamp Student Union.
The historic Cole Field House arena — home of Terps basketball until 2002 — rebuilt as the Jones-Hill House complex with football operations, sports medicine, and innovation spaces.
South campus's all-you-care-to-eat dining hall, serving residents of South Hill, South Campus Commons, and anyone on a dining plan.
North campus dining hall in the Denton community, known as “251 North,” with all-you-care-to-eat stations.
